# Research & knowledge

Literature search, citation mapping, document chat, source-grounded notebooks, and answer engines. These tools can shorten the path to a useful source, but they can also summarize confidently and get details wrong. Open the original paper, report, or document before you cite it.

**Last verified:** October 22, 2026 · **14 tools**

[Back to the guide](../README.md) · [All categories](README.md) · [Safety checklist](../free-tier-safety.md)

> **Category tip:** Never cite a paper based only on a generated summary. Check the authors, publication venue, date, methods, and whether the quoted passage actually supports your claim. Avoid uploading confidential research data or personal information to free services; use institution-approved tools when a study requires it.

**Start here:** [NotebookLM](#tool-notebooklm) · [Elicit](#tool-elicit) · [Semantic Scholar](#tool-semantic-scholar)

## All 14 tools

<a id="tool-elicit"></a>

### Elicit

`Free tier` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free monthly credit allowance for AI-assisted literature search, paper screening, and structured extraction from research papers.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free account; no card. Monthly credits limit searches and extractions.
- **Limits:** Credits limit searches, extractions, and larger reviews. Advanced columns, team features, and high volume are paid. Results need verification against the original papers.
- **Best for:** Getting from a research question to a shortlist of relevant papers and a structured comparison.
- **Official link:** <https://elicit.com>
- **Tags:** `literature-review` `papers` `extraction` `academic`

---

<a id="tool-consensus"></a>

### Consensus

`Free tier` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** Free AI-powered search across scientific papers with claim summaries, citation context, and links to the underlying studies.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free account or sign-in; no card expected. Free searches and synthesis features are capped.
- **Limits:** Free searches and advanced synthesis are capped. The best-use answer is a starting point, not a systematic review. Study quality varies and must be appraised.
- **Best for:** Asking what the research literature says about a focused yes/no or comparison question.
- **Official link:** <https://consensus.app>
- **Tags:** `evidence` `papers` `summaries` `citations`

---

<a id="tool-semantic-scholar"></a>

### Semantic Scholar

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** Free scholarly search with AI-generated paper summaries, citation context, author pages, and links to related work.
- **Sign-up notes:** No account for basic search; an optional free account adds features. No card.
- **Limits:** Search and the website are free; bulk API use is rate-limited. Summaries can omit important limitations, and full-text access depends on publisher permissions.
- **Best for:** Broad academic discovery and quick paper triage with fewer distractions than a general search engine.
- **Official link:** <https://www.semanticscholar.org>
- **Tags:** `papers` `citations` `summaries` `academic`

---

<a id="tool-connected-papers"></a>

### Connected Papers

`Free tier` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** Free visual citation graphs that show related papers around one seed paper, with a small monthly graph allowance.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free account; no card. Monthly graph allowances apply.
- **Limits:** Free graphs per month are limited, and the tool maps relationships rather than judging quality. Some features and larger use require a subscription.
- **Best for:** Getting oriented in an unfamiliar field by seeing which papers cluster around a key work.
- **Official link:** <https://www.connectedpapers.com>
- **Tags:** `citations` `visualization` `discovery` `academic`

---

<a id="tool-researchrabbit"></a>

### ResearchRabbit

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** Free literature discovery, citation maps, author tracking, and collections designed to grow as your reading list grows.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free account, often via Google sign-in; no card. The free discovery tools may change over time.
- **Limits:** Its recommendations are only as good as the metadata and are not a quality judgment. Features may change, and very large collections or integrations can be constrained.
- **Best for:** Mapping a literature neighborhood and keeping track of papers over time without paying.
- **Official link:** <https://www.researchrabbit.ai>
- **Tags:** `discovery` `citation-maps` `collections` `free`

---

<a id="tool-litmaps"></a>

### Litmaps

`Free tier` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free plan for citation maps, literature discovery, and limited saved maps and alerts.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free account; no card. Saved maps and alerts are limited.
- **Limits:** Free map, search, alert, and export allowances are small. Paid plans support larger libraries and more collaboration. Always check the cited source.
- **Best for:** Visual researchers who want to track new papers in a field and see how work connects.
- **Official link:** <https://www.litmaps.com>
- **Tags:** `citation-maps` `alerts` `literature` `discovery`

---

<a id="tool-notebooklm"></a>

### NotebookLM

`Free tier` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** Google's source-grounded notebook for uploading documents, linking sources, asking questions, generating study guides, and making limited audio overviews.
- **Sign-up notes:** Google account; no card. Daily questions, sources, and audio overviews are capped.
- **Limits:** Notebooks, sources, daily questions, and audio/video overviews have caps. The model answers from the sources you add, but its interpretation can still be wrong. Avoid private data.
- **Best for:** Studying a focused set of PDFs, notes, or articles and asking questions with citations back to the uploads.
- **Official link:** <https://notebooklm.google.com>
- **Tags:** `documents` `study` `citations` `audio-overview`

---

<a id="tool-chatpdf"></a>

### ChatPDF

`Free tier` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** Chat with uploaded PDFs and get answers with page references on a free daily allowance.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free account for saved PDFs; no card. Page, upload, and question limits apply.
- **Limits:** Free uploads, page counts, and daily questions are limited. Files go to a third-party service, so do not upload manuscripts, private records, or patient documents without permission.
- **Best for:** Asking quick orientation questions about a paper or report before a careful full read.
- **Official link:** <https://www.chatpdf.com>
- **Tags:** `pdf` `chat` `documents` `reading`

---

<a id="tool-scispace"></a>

### SciSpace

`Free tier` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free monthly allowance of AI credits for chatting with papers, explaining math and jargon, and discovering related literature.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free account; no card. Monthly AI credits and upload limits apply.
- **Limits:** AI credits, uploads, and premium tools are limited or paid. Summaries can miss nuance, and uploaded papers can be handled by third parties. Verify every citation.
- **Best for:** Reading outside your field and getting plain-language help with dense methods or equations.
- **Official link:** <https://scispace.com>
- **Tags:** `papers` `explanations` `pdf` `academic`

---

<a id="tool-phind"></a>

### Phind

`Free tier` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** AI answers with web citations aimed at technical and developer questions, with a limited free allowance of advanced model searches.
- **Sign-up notes:** Basic search may work without an account; no card. Advanced model searches are capped with sign-in.
- **Limits:** Advanced searches and larger models have daily/per-feature caps. Answers can miss current issues or cite weak sources. It is not a substitute for documentation and tests.
- **Best for:** Debugging questions and technical research where you want links to current docs and discussions.
- **Official link:** <https://www.phind.com>
- **Tags:** `technical` `coding` `web-search` `citations`

---

<a id="tool-storm"></a>

### STORM

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free Stanford research prototype that interviews you, gathers web sources, and drafts a Wikipedia-style report with citations.
- **Sign-up notes:** No account required for the public prototype; no card. Runs and availability are limited.
- **Limits:** Research runs are limited and the tool is experimental. Citations can be incomplete or misapplied, and the report still needs editing. Do not treat it as peer-reviewed work.
- **Best for:** Rapidly assembling a broad reading outline on a new topic before deeper research.
- **Official link:** <https://storm.genie.stanford.edu>
- **Tags:** `report-generation` `web-research` `citations` `experimental`

---

<a id="tool-explainpaper"></a>

### Explainpaper

`Free tier` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** Upload a research paper, highlight difficult text, and get an AI explanation of that passage in simpler language.
- **Sign-up notes:** Free account; no card. Free document and question limits apply.
- **Limits:** Free document and question allowances are limited; advanced features and higher usage are paid. Explanations can be wrong, especially for statistics and domain-specific methods.
- **Best for:** Getting unstuck on a dense paragraph without leaving the paper.
- **Official link:** <https://www.explainpaper.com>
- **Tags:** `papers` `explanations` `students` `reading`

<a id="tool-inciteful"></a>

### Inciteful

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** Free citation-graph and literature-discovery tools that help you find influential papers connected to a seed paper or topic.
- **Sign-up notes:** No account required for basic use; no card. Rate limits and prototype availability apply.
- **Limits:** The service is donation/education-oriented, with possible rate limits and incomplete metadata. It surfaces candidates, not proof that a source is high quality.
- **Best for:** Exploring citation trails and finding older or adjacent papers that keyword search misses.
- **Official link:** <https://inciteful.xyz>
- **Tags:** `citations` `discovery` `no-account` `academic`

<a id="tool-ai2-paper-finder"></a>

### Ai2 Paper Finder

`Free` · Last verified: 2026-10-22

- **What is free:** A free AI-assisted literature-search prototype from the Allen Institute for AI that iteratively searches for niche or hard-to-find papers.
- **Sign-up notes:** Public research prototype; no account or card expected. Availability can vary.
- **Limits:** It is a research prototype, so availability, speed, and result quality can vary. It finds candidates; it does not read, appraise, or cite them for you.
- **Best for:** Finding hard-to-describe papers when ordinary keyword search keeps missing the mark.
- **Official link:** <https://paperfinder.allen.ai>
- **Tags:** `literature-search` `ai2` `free` `academic`
